desc:
A walker starts at (0, 0) and must reach (a, b) using unit steps to the right (x + 1) or up (y + 1). Count the routes on which every visited point satisfies y ≤ x, so the route never rises above the diagonal. Return the count modulo 1,000,000,007.

a = 2, b = 1 -> 2    (RRU and RUR; URR goes above the diagonal)
a = 3, b = 3 -> 5    (the Catalan number C3)
hints: Count all routes to (a, b) first: that is a binomial coefficient. Then subtract the routes that touch the forbidden line y = x + 1.
Reflect the start point across the forbidden line y = x + 1. Routes that touch the line correspond one-to-one with routes from the reflected start to (a, b).
The reflected start is (-1, 1), which needs a + b + 1 steps with b ups and a + 1 rights, so the bad routes number C(a + b, b - 1).
editorial: All routes from (0, 0) to (a, b) use a right steps and b up steps, so there are C(a + b, b) of them. Some of these touch the line y = x + 1, which is the first point where a route leaves the allowed region.

By the reflection principle, the bad routes correspond to routes from the mirror image of the start, (-1, 1), to (a, b). Those have a + 1 right steps and b - 1 up steps, so there are C(a + b, b - 1) of them. The answer is C(a + b, b) - C(a + b, b - 1), the ballot number.
Precompute factorials up to a + b and use modular inverses through Fermat's little theorem. Setting a = b = n gives the Catalan number Cn, which is a useful check.
